title: StoryLark presentation
description: The shape of a StoryLark library: how it is organised, what a content unit is called, and how the shell is arranged. Every key is optional — an absent key takes the core default, permanently, so a template written today keeps working on every future engine, and an unknown key is ignored with a warning so a template written for a NEWER engine loads on an older one. The complete default for every key is DEFAULT_PRESENTATION in storylark-core/src/presentation.ts; this file states what is LEGAL, that one states what is CHOSEN when nothing is said. `contractVersion` does not move when a backwards-compatible key is added here — the two rules above already cover that case — only on a genuinely breaking reshape.

contractVersion.description: Contract major version. The engine refuses a file whose major it does not support; see SUPPORTED_CONTRACT_VERSION in validate.mjs.

layout.description: Library shape. 'flat' — standalone units in one list, no collection level. 'series' — units grouped into collections.

nouns.description: What a content unit and its collection are called throughout the UI. No user-visible string hardcodes 'story' or 'book'.

collection.description: The grouping level's name ('book', 'series'), or null for a flat library.

items.description: Which navigation entries appear, and in what order.

labels.description: Optional per-item label override; defaults come from `nouns`.

sections.description: Presence in the list = shown; order = display order.

defaultSort.description: How units are ordered within a section. 'order' is the reading order the author intends (manifest order); 'timeframe' is the in-world chronology; 'recent' is real-world release date, newest first.

sortOptions.description: Which sorts the picker offers, and in what order. An empty array removes the picker. A timeframe sort is meaningful for an in-world chronology and meaningless elsewhere, which is why the OFFER is configurable and not only the default.

groupBy.description: How units are divided into sections. 'collection' is the collection level (a series, or the `group` when there is no series); 'group' is the era/collection label on each unit; 'timeframe' is the in-world period.

groupOptions.description: Which groupings the picker offers alongside the sorts.

view.description: 'list' — one row per unit. 'grid' — a cover shelf.

defaultMode.description: How an item opens when a reader who has expressed no preference taps it. A reader who HAS chosen keeps their choice — this is the deployment's default, not an override.

cover.description: Cover shape on the shelves. A short-story library with square title illustrations and a book publisher with portrait covers want visibly different shelves.

detail.description: Which parts of the unit/collection detail screen appear. A one-chapter short story and a 20-chapter book want different detail pages.

showLength.description: Reading time / narration duration on each row.

auth.description: Sign-in posture. A genuine per-deployment decision, not a reader preference: it changes the whole first-run experience.

required.description: true puts an account gate in front of the whole app; false is browse-and-read anonymously.

readerTheme.description: Which of the bundled sample LOOKS a reader may read in. A look is the colours and font stacks of one of the gallery themes and nothing else — it never changes this deployment's identity, icons, PWA manifest or installed theme package, and one reader's choice is never visible to another. `settings.theme` still gates the whole Theme control: turning that off removes this too.

options.description: Which looks the picker offers, in this order. An empty array removes the picker and leaves every reader on this library's own theme.css. An id this engine does not ship is ignored, so a file written for a newer engine still offers the looks it does have.

forced.description: Fix one look for every reader. The picker becomes a read-only line, `options` is ignored, and a reader who had already chosen something else is moved onto this one — a forced look overrides a stored preference rather than merely hiding the control. null (the default) leaves readers to choose.

settings.description: Which controls the Settings screen offers the reader. An opinionated brand may not want its look overridable; an accessibility-minded one very much does.

narrator.description: Narrator picker (still only shown when the library publishes two or more voices).

autoPlay.description: Auto-play the next unit (still only shown when auto-download is per-unit).

download.description: What auto-download means here. Previously DERIVED from `layout`, which was surprising and undocumented in the UI; it is an explicit choice now, defaulting to whatever the layout used to imply.

mode.description: 'newUnits' — only units published after the reader turned the toggle on. 'everything' — the whole library, including new units as they publish.

emptyState.description: First-run and empty-shelf copy — the very first thing a new deployment shows its owner. `{unit}`, `{unitPlural}`, `{Unit}`, `{UnitPlural}`, `{collection}`, `{Collection}` and (in `librarySearch`) `{query}` are substituted from `nouns`.

about.description: Extra links and credits, so a brand can point at its own site, licence, or contact.

features.description: Where every new core feature lands. An open map on purpose: a feature core has not shipped yet is not an unknown key, and a feature a template predates simply takes the core default.
